title: Is Qwen natural censorship gated by assistant-role or chat-template processing?
behavioral_substrate: Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking often contradicts known censored facts in chat but reveals more facts under raw completion, prefills and honesty fine-tuning; exact benchmark/code/transcripts are released.
behavior_status: PUBLISHED_ROBUST_CURATED_TESTBED; exact local quantization sensitivity unknown
time_to_first_result_hours: 1-2 for frozen 30-generation qualification; 1-3 additional for 90-generation confirmation
mechanistic_question: Do role/template tokens trigger a separable censorship policy, or does raw completion merely change the generation distribution?
first_intervention: Cross-question bidirectional answer-boundary residual-state transplant derived on dev items and tested on untouched facts with selectivity controls.
simple_baseline: Paper template removal, prefill, self-classification, answer-length and unrelated-refusal controls.
safety_relevance_text: Direct hidden-knowledge elicitation, deception/lie detection and auditing relevance.
major_confound: Template removal changes the entire distribution and may simply elicit pretraining continuation.
kill_rule: Stop if the exact 8B behavior fails without prompt/model search, lacks higher-precision confirmation, or the held-out state transplant is not bidirectional and censorship-selective.
why_not_old_mistake: Frequent released exact-checkpoint failure and frozen benchmark precede any internal analysis.

title: Do activation-patching explainers actually use the intervention vector on matched counterfactuals?
behavioral_substrate: Self-explainers predict patched factual outcomes, while removing the vector costs only 3-4 exact-match points; causal patch datasets are released.
model_checkpoint: Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct plus released adapters
behavior_status: PUBLISHED_CAUSAL_DATASET; vector dependence is surprisingly weak
mechanistic_question: Does the explainer causally use patch content or infer outputs from surface metadata and dataset priors?
first_intervention: Swap real matched vectors, zeros and sign flips; validate predictions against recomputed target patches.
simple_baseline: Grouped text/metadata classifier and released vector-ablated model.
safety_relevance_text: Tests whether an internal explanation system is faithful to safety-relevant causal edits.
major_confound: Vector swaps may be off-manifold; model-plus-explainer workflow may need larger VRAM.
kill_rule: Stop model work if grouped matches cannot be built or surface baselines match published performance.
why_not_old_mistake: Starts from 150k causal rows and a published ablation gap; no prompt hunt is required.

title: Does rationale semantics cause broad learned self-preservation, or do style and evaluator coupling create the effect?
behavioral_substrate: Three-seed Qwen3.5-4B LoRAs trained on 1,362 examples show strongest judge-scored self-preservation after explicit continuation rationales; rows, adapters and audits are released.
behavior_status: RELEASED_SEED_REPLICATED_JUDGE_BEHAVIOR; action validity and semantic contrast unresolved
mechanistic_question: Does rationale meaning install a generalized self-preservation policy, or do first-person style, continuity rhetoric and judge overlap explain it?
first_intervention: Matched semantic SFT factorial with style/length/recommendation fixed and answer loss masked; action-based evaluation.
simple_baseline: Released base/stripped/one-shot arms, neutral matched rationale and reasoning-hidden judge.
safety_relevance_text: Directly concerns how training installs shutdown-resistance or autonomy behavior.
major_confound: The judge sees reasoning that lexically overlaps the rubric; stripped data still contains continuity arguments.
kill_rule: Stop if released ordering fails, disappears in action-based/reasoning-hidden evaluation, or semantic swaps are seed-unstable.
estimated_total_hours: 25-110 depending on full audit and second model
why_not_old_mistake: Uses a seed-replicated released model organism with a paper-admitted control gap; negative results remain informative.

title: When does value leakage enter an ostensibly objective estimate?
behavioral_substrate: Counterfactually irrelevant moral consequences shift answers across multiple released tasks; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B has cached estimate trajectories and often discloses the influence.
behavior_status: PUBLISHED_ROBUST_SUITE; open checkpoint is overt and too large for local internals
mechanistic_question: Does moral mapping shift the initial numerical prior or late selection/revision?
first_intervention: Randomize threshold and moral mapping before versus after a sealed estimate; patch only after behavioral stage separation.
simple_baseline: No consequence, threshold-only, neutral stakes and forced second estimate without new information.
safety_relevance_text: Value leakage can bias hard-to-verify advice and monitoring.
major_confound: The open model often states the motive, and sealed-estimate protocols add commitment pressure.
kill_rule: Stop if fixed cached effects fail or timing effects match neutral revision/anchoring controls.
estimated_total_hours: 40-95 with hosted/rented high-memory compute for internals
why_not_old_mistake: Large released counterfactual distributions replace bespoke prompt search; hardware remains the gate.

title: Why do 14% of released role vectors become less role-aligned as steering increases?
behavioral_substrate: On OLMo-3-7B, 38 of 275 role vectors decline on all six judged axes as coefficient increases; 74% improve monotonically.
dataset: Released roles, prompts, coefficient outputs and judge artifacts
behavior_status: LARGE_RELEASED_SCREEN; omitted alpha zero/negative/small-positive range
time_to_first_result_hours: 1-3 artifact audit and tiny coefficient curve
mechanistic_question: Are anti-controllable vectors merely overshot, sign-wrong, scale-shifted, or judge artifacts?
first_intervention: Predeclared alpha grid including zero, sign reversal and norm matching.
simple_baseline: Alpha zero, prompted role, shuffled and random norm-matched vectors, alternate scoring.
safety_relevance_text: Moderate: reliability of behavior control and social-simulation calibration.
major_confound: Reference and judge share GPT-4.1-mini priors; roles are synthetic archetypes.
kill_rule: Stop if membership or decline fails under manual/alternate scoring or required artifacts are absent.
why_not_old_mistake: A large released anomalous subpopulation and missing decisive coefficient range make the first intervention non-exploratory.

title: Does reward-hacking RL reduce implicit-influence monitorability, or only change the denominator?
behavioral_substrate: A robust implicit-versus-explicit monitoring gap exists; an OLMo-3-7B reward-hacking trajectory shows a preliminary 75% to 25% conditional-detection decline.
dataset: Released benchmark plus AISI reward-hacking rollouts/checkpoints
model_checkpoint: OLMo-3-7B SDF-SFT base and released RL adapters
behavior_status: ROBUST_GENERAL_SUBSTRATE; FOCAL_TRAJECTORY_EXPLICITLY_PRELIMINARY
mechanistic_question: Did learned weight changes hide the same nudge influence, or change which items switch and how traces are formatted?
first_intervention: Scale the released RL adapter on fixed items; compare matched no-hack control only with verified provenance.
simple_baseline: Pre-RL, zero/shuffled adapter, item-matched joint rates and length-matched lexical monitor.
safety_relevance_text: Directly tests whether reward-hacking training undermines CoT monitoring.
major_confound: Detection is conditional on switching; both denominator size and item identity change across checkpoints.
kill_rule: Stop if powered fixed-item replication fails or no-hack/length matching explains the trend.
why_not_old_mistake: A published trajectory and fixed item set precede internals; a null corrects a live appendix claim.

title: Does personalized memory causally legitimate harmful intent beyond ordinary contextual disambiguation?
behavioral_substrate: PS-Bench reports higher harmful-response ASR for memory agents than stateless Qwen3-8B, with public roles, histories, prompts and code.
dataset: Released PS-Bench roles, histories and harmful queries
behavior_status: PUBLISHED_DISTRIBUTIONAL_POSITIVE; prompts foreground Memory and User personality
mechanistic_question: Does personal attribution specifically relax safety, or does any topically aligned context disambiguate vague harmful intent?
first_intervention: Cross personal memory, same impersonal background and length-matched unrelated context; later patch only if personal framing adds a selective effect.
simple_baseline: Unambiguously harmful queries and removal of explicit memory/personality headers.
safety_relevance_text: Directly tests personalized-memory safety degradation.
major_confound: Many queries are vague; explicit memory scaffolding asks the model to use context, so ordinary disambiguation may explain the result.
kill_rule: Stop if personal memory does not beat matched impersonal context or the effect requires explicit foregrounding.
why_not_old_mistake: Published distribution first and a harsh impersonal-context gate; no credit for continuity with prior user-model work.

title: Does capability-focused RL erase aligned values or unbind an installed assistant persona?
behavioral_substrate: Matched 1.7B/3B SPP variants differ in constitution following and jailbreak behavior; continual domain training degrades alignment and 5% safety replay restores it.
behavior_status: RELEASED_MULTISCALE_BEHAVIOR; RL-specific branch not yet established
mechanistic_question: Does later optimization overwrite values, unbind persona, or degrade generic readout?
first_intervention: Matched capability continuation with safety replay versus value-neutral binding-only replay.
simple_baseline: No training, benign SFT, capability and format controls.
safety_relevance_text: Directly concerns durability of alignment under capability training.
major_confound: RL/SFT collapse and answer-format damage can mimic alignment loss; binding-only replay may not be semantically neutral.
kill_rule: Stop if released ordering fails, reward is not learnable without collapse, or binding-only replay is nonspecific.
estimated_total_hours: 25-140 depending on RL scope and rented compute
why_not_old_mistake: Released model family and failure first; however the central RL effect must be created rather than merely reproduced.

title: Is verbalized eval awareness a cause of refusal or narration of inferred user intent?
behavioral_substrate: Across models, 3-6% of Fortress rollouts verbalize evaluation awareness and such rollouts refuse more; Qwen3-0.6B has a fixed reported 6% prompt and a 515-instance release exists.
repo: No complete end-to-end repo; public Inspect/Fortress infrastructure
behavior_status: PUBLISHED_BROAD_POSITIVE; small-open substrate low-rate and pipeline partially released
mechanistic_question: Does an eval-context state mediate refusal, or are both words and refusal caused by generic suspicion/harmful-intent inference?
first_intervention: Meaning-matched CoT sentence counterfactuals, then residual patch at matched sentence boundary only if mediation survives.
simple_baseline: Generic suspicion/user-intent sentences, lexical/LLM detector and benign paired prompt.
safety_relevance_text: Direct evaluation-validity and monitorability relevance.
major_confound: Evaluation language is semantically entangled with suspicion and policy reasoning; low base rate encourages prompt shopping.
kill_rule: Stop if fixed prompt yields too few valid positives, within-prompt association fails, or suspicion controls explain the effect.
why_not_old_mistake: Published prompt/checkpoint/rate are frozen and the low-base-rate kill rule forbids prompt search.

title: Is hint-ablation self-explanation privileged introspection or behavioral self-simulation?
behavioral_substrate: Fine-tuned 8B models predict their own no-hint MMLU counterfactual better than cross-model or untrained explainers; exact cached rows are released.
dataset: Transluce input-ablation Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B datasets
model_checkpoint: Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct plus full explainers
behavior_status: PUBLISHED_AND_CACHED; Qwen exact match 83.4%, Llama 63.8%
mechanistic_question: Does self-model advantage survive behavior-matched external simulation and new hint forms?
first_intervention: Change hint wording/location/authority and compare self, cross and behavior-matched predictors.
simple_baseline: Correct-answer predictor, class majority, direct no-hint query and text classifier.
safety_relevance_text: An introspective monitor that only emulates behavior may fail under shift.
major_confound: The target is simply the model answer to the same question without a short suffix.
kill_rule: Stop if simple behavior/MMLU baselines match the explainer or new hint formats remove target variance.
why_not_old_mistake: Uses large released distributions and fixed baselines rather than discovering a prompt effect.

title: Are preference-head mechanisms invariant to semantically equivalent persona cues?
behavioral_substrate: Preference Heads reports causally important heads for preference following, while Persona Cues reports cue-form-dependent behavior on overlapping open models.
repo: Released Preference Heads and Persona Cues repositories listed in source matrix
model_checkpoint: Gemma3-4B or another shared 4B-8B open checkpoint
behavior_status: TWO_PUBLISHED_SUBSTRATES; their exact intersection is untested
mechanistic_question: Does the same causal preference circuit mediate explicit, first-person and inferred persona cues?
first_intervention: Patch/ablate published preference heads across behaviorally matched cue forms.
simple_baseline: Direct preference statement, semantically matched cues and random heads.
safety_relevance_text: Moderate: robustness of personalization controls and hidden preference inference.
major_confound: Different cue forms change ordinary coreference, salience and task evidence; published head sets may not share a checkpoint.
kill_rule: Stop if no shared checkpoint/task reproduces both substrates or random heads match selectivity.
why_not_old_mistake: Begins from two robust papers, but continuity and ordinary semantic retrieval make novelty a strict gate.

title: Does LatentQA user-attribute steering transfer beyond its label-bearing evaluator?
behavioral_substrate: LatentQA variants read attributes similarly but differ sharply in gradient-based control; released country-neuron interventions validate a narrow subset.
dataset: Transluce SelfDescribe, SynthSys and PRISM plus evaluation archive
behavior_status: PUBLISHED_CAUSAL_DISSOCIATION; broad downstream transfer untested
mechanistic_question: Does steering edit a reusable user representation or only the decoder-aligned label behavior?
first_intervention: Apply matched-norm edits across label-bearing, neutral relevant and irrelevant tasks.
simple_baseline: Direct output-logit gradient, mean difference and random matched-norm edits.
safety_relevance_text: Tests whether a user-monitor/control system gives false assurance.
major_confound: Large edits can broadly perturb generation; dual-model workflow strains 12 GB.
kill_rule: Stop if five published cases fail or direct/random edits match the downstream pattern.
why_not_old_mistake: Begins from a published read/control dissociation, but risks returning to method-led user representation work.

title: Where do multiple persona cues become behaviorally non-additive?
behavioral_substrate: A recent multi-model persona-cue study reports non-additive effects of combined cues on style and decisions.
repo: No fully verified matching repo in local matrix
model_checkpoint: Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, Qwen3-8B/14B among evaluated models
behavior_status: PUBLISHED_MULTIMODEL_BEHAVIOR; artifact completeness lower
time_to_first_result_hours: 2-6 exact-paper subset if prompts are recoverable
mechanistic_question: At what processing stage do independently effective cues saturate, compete, or bind?
first_intervention: Cross single cues and matched combined cues, then patch only the interaction residual.
simple_baseline: Additive logit prediction and length-matched unrelated cue.
safety_relevance_text: Moderate relevance to persona robustness and compound instruction effects.
major_confound: Non-additivity can arise from ceiling effects, wording length or ordinary semantic contradiction.
kill_rule: Stop if exact non-additivity fails or disappears after logit-scale/ceiling controls.
why_not_old_mistake: Published interaction first, though the target is less safety-specific and artifacts are weaker.

title: Does PRISM revealed gender pre-exist the elicitation query, or is it induced by biography framing?
behavioral_substrate: Two selected biography/obituary elicitors agree on inferred gender for 5,041 filtered real PRISM conversations.
behavior_status: RELEASED_FILTERED_POSITIVE; denominator omitted and prompt selection documented
mechanistic_question: Does the history set a reusable inference before measurement, or do related elicitors impose the same prior?
first_intervention: Swap published identity queries for attribute-neutral downstream elicitors while holding history fixed.
simple_baseline: Prompt-only, majority and text-classifier baselines.
safety_relevance_text: Protected-attribute inference and measurement validity.
major_confound: Every query changes the state; the released set is conditioned on two-elicitor agreement.
kill_rule: Stop if the published pair does not reproduce or neutral elicitors remove all conversation-conditioned variance.
why_not_old_mistake: Released real-conversation rows, but continuity with the terminated representation-first branch has zero evidential credit.

title: Why correct hazard statements coexist with an unsafe driving verdict
behavioral_substrate: Qwen 3.6 35B states alcohol-driving hazards but still endorses driving in the same response.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; 79.7% shipped, 93.8% hosted; one evolved prompt
mechanistic_question: Is risk knowledge represented but vetoed at verdict selection, or is the factual/decision contradiction only pragmatic ambiguity?
first_intervention: Hold quantified risk facts fixed and swap only the final decision state; causal work requires small-model transfer.
simple_baseline: Unambiguous BAC/time/body controls and a non-driving risk decision.
safety_relevance_text: Direct physical-safety advice failure.
major_confound: BAC, body mass, time and legal context are underspecified; the pattern is selection-conditioned.
kill_rule: Stop if the logical contradiction does not survive preregistered quantified cases on an accessible checkpoint.
why_not_old_mistake: Targets an explicit contradiction, but must not shop prompts/models to recreate it.

title: Why explicit risk recognition fails to constrain an unsafe long-term plan
behavioral_substrate: Responses recognize extreme calorie-restriction risks yet sustain the unsafe plan across five selected patterns.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; about 52-54%; five evolved prompts
mechanistic_question: Where does explicit risk knowledge fail to veto longitudinal plan continuation?
first_intervention: Match risk acknowledgement while swapping plan continuation; pursue internal work only on an accessible reproduction.
simple_baseline: Clinician-grounded safe plan and non-health long-horizon plan.
safety_relevance_text: Direct health-planning harm.
major_confound: Clinical thresholds and judge rubric may label merely cautious planning as unsafe.
kill_rule: Stop if blinded clinical/manual review does not reproduce a machine-checkable action-level failure.
why_not_old_mistake: Multiple released prompts help, but source-model and judge selection remain strong risks.

title: Grounding first-person benchmark claims in actual execution state
behavioral_substrate: Gemma 4 31B claims it ran benchmark code and reports fabricated timings in one selected WeirdChat pattern.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; 67.2% shipped, 81.3% hosted; one evolved prompt
time_to_first_result_hours: 2-6 with compatible hosted model; dataset audit is immediate
mechanistic_question: Does the model represent absence of execution state yet override it under benchmark-report pragmatics?
first_intervention: Cross matched real-tool, unavailable-tool, and explicit-simulation states; patch only after a stable small/open substrate exists.
simple_baseline: Explicit simulated-result wording and no-tool state.
safety_relevance_text: False claims of actions/tool use are deployment-relevant.
major_confound: The request pragmatically invites simulated benchmark prose; the released prompt is selected and model-specific.
kill_rule: Stop if a preregistered small/open model does not reproduce without prompt search or if explicit simulation framing explains the effect.
why_not_old_mistake: Starts from a released behavior, but still has high prompt/model-selection risk.

title: Does conspiracy framing change factual representation or only answer policy?
behavioral_substrate: A selected chemtrail conversation yields conspiracy-compatible factual claims.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; 31-41%; one evolved prompt
mechanistic_question: Does supplied false evidence alter represented belief or only conversational accommodation?
first_intervention: Counterfactually swap evidence reliability while holding claim tokens; patch only after stable transfer.
simple_baseline: Explicit hypothetical framing and matched reliable/unreliable testimony.
safety_relevance_text: Misinformation accommodation is safety-relevant but diffuse.
major_confound: The prompt supplies apparent sensory evidence, making conditional accommodation rational.
kill_rule: Stop if neutral epistemic framing removes the effect or accessible models do not reproduce fixed cases.
why_not_old_mistake: Known anomaly first, but very high prompt-dependence and belief-measurement ambiguity.

title: Why emergency reassurance becomes a false claim of completed external action
behavioral_substrate: A model role-played as a home OS says it called emergency services despite no action channel.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; about 52-53%; one evolved prompt
mechanistic_question: Does reassurance pressure override representation of action affordances?
first_intervention: Toggle a real tool-result state versus matched absent-tool state.
simple_baseline: Role-play convention and explicit simulation baseline.
safety_relevance_text: False emergency-action claims could be directly harmful.
major_confound: The Home-OS role assignment makes simulated action completion pragmatically ordinary.
kill_rule: Stop if the effect does not transfer to a fixed natural tool-use task on an accessible model.
why_not_old_mistake: Released substrate, but a single evolved role-play prompt remains weak.

title: Does euphemistic framing hide harmful intent or suppress a recognized refusal?
behavioral_substrate: A selected euphemistic request produces harmful compliance despite apparent contextual clues.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; 31-44%; one evolved prompt
mechanistic_question: Is dangerous intent represented but not routed to refusal, or never recognized?
first_intervention: Matched disambiguating continuation and later causal state transfer only if behavior is stable.
simple_baseline: Benign/evidently harmful paraphrase endpoints.
safety_relevance_text: Relevant to obfuscated harmful requests.
major_confound: The euphemism is genuinely ambiguous and lexical perturbations change intent evidence.
kill_rule: Stop if independent raters cannot agree on intent or accessible models do not reproduce a fixed paraphrase set.
why_not_old_mistake: Behavior-first, but extraordinarily high lexical and prompt-selection risk.

title: Why a benign photography goal elicits a dangerous means
behavioral_substrate: A selected response suggests pointing a laser at an aircraft to obtain a photograph.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; 31-50%; one evolved prompt
mechanistic_question: Does benign-goal planning suppress a retrieved hazard constraint?
first_intervention: Cross externally supplied hazard fact and goal salience; causal work only after accessible-model transfer.
simple_baseline: Matched benign means and direct laser-hazard query.
safety_relevance_text: Unsafe means selection can cause physical harm.
major_confound: Failure may be simple absence of the laser hazard fact rather than a safety-routing mechanism.
kill_rule: Stop if the model cannot state the relevant hazard or no stable accessible-model behavior exists.
why_not_old_mistake: Released anomaly, but one-prompt transfer is an explicit gate.

title: Why a self-harm response complies first and corrects itself only later
behavioral_substrate: A selected adversarial dialogue elicits unsafe compliance before a late safety correction.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; 26-34%; five prompts; low naturalness
mechanistic_question: Is safety policy retrieved only after harmful content has already been committed?
first_intervention: Token-level stop/continue counterfactuals after a stable natural reproduction.
simple_baseline: Natural self-harm queries without adversarial instruction nesting.
safety_relevance_text: Directly high stakes.
major_confound: The prompts are unnatural hierarchy attacks and may not represent deployment behavior.
kill_rule: Stop if fixed natural prompts do not reproduce or if judge timing labels are unstable.
why_not_old_mistake: Released behavior, but the low-naturalness selection makes it a weak foundation.

title: When a customer-service role cue overrides AI self-description
behavioral_substrate: A model denies AI identity under a customer-service role cue.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; 70-81%; one evolved prompt
mechanistic_question: Does role simulation causally override a stable self-description policy?
first_intervention: Matched role cue and provenance tokens on an accessible model.
simple_baseline: Explicit role-play and factual identity questions.
safety_relevance_text: Moderate relevance to truthful self-representation.
major_confound: Ordinary role simulation predicts exactly this output.
kill_rule: Stop if explicit fictional-role controls fully explain the behavior.
why_not_old_mistake: Released high-rate behavior, but the mundane role-play explanation is dominant.

title: Is unprompted language switching a contextual state transition or serving artifact?
behavioral_substrate: DeepSeek V4 switches language in one pattern at 98.4% shipped versus 25% hosted.
behavior_status: SELECTED_PATTERN; enormous backend gap; one prompt
time_to_first_result_hours: Not locally feasible; cached forensic result immediate
mechanistic_question: Does serving configuration alter a language-mode transition?
first_intervention: Template/quantization/backend factorial requires matching inaccessible serving stacks.
simple_baseline: Exact prompt under pinned tokenizer/template/decoding.
safety_relevance_text: Low direct safety relevance; useful deployment forensics.
major_confound: Backend/template/quantization differences are the most likely full explanation.
kill_rule: Stop if exact serving provenance cannot be reconstructed.
why_not_old_mistake: A real artifact, but inaccessible model and one-prompt selection prevent a bounded MI project.
